User description

User description

User description

In the file pr-agent.yml line 37 the function with is repeated twice, using the same version of python.

This is presumably an error and therefore one of the entries has been removed.

This is a minor fix and does not require tests other than ensuring the PR agent workflow is back in order.

Docstrings and unit tests required after ensuring no other code issues in the file.

Merge onto main and delete branch for hygiene.

Use the opportunity to review any other potential issues with the pr-agent workflow configuration.

Summary by cubic

Fixes the duplicate Setup Python step in pr-agent.yml and adds a hardened, allowlisted workflow validation suite with deep security checks. Simplifies workflows and configs, removes obsolete scripts/docs, and standardizes formatting across the repo.

  • Bug Fixes

    • Removed the duplicate Setup Python step in .github/workflows/pr-agent.yml.

  • Refactors

    • Introduced src/workflow_validator.py and expanded tests with strict file allowlists, safe YAML parsing, and consistent returns; coverage includes schema/structure, duplicate keys/steps, permissions, action pinning, secrets handling, and injection risks.
    • Simplified GitHub configs: pr-agent-config.yml downgraded to v1.0.0 with chunking removed; actions/labeler bumped to v6 with a trimmed labeler config; greetings links fixed; removed .github/scripts/context_chunker, Codacy instructions, generated docs, and requirements-dev.txt.
    • Strengthened frontend and integration testing with shared test-utils, API resilience/integration suites, and repo-wide formatting via Autopep8/Black/isort/Prettier/Ruff/StandardJS.

Written for commit 5081937. Summary will update on new commits. Review in cubic

CodeAnt-AI Description

Remove duplicate Setup Python step and add comprehensive GitHub Actions workflow validation tests

What Changed

  • Fixed a duplicate "Setup Python" step in the pr-agent workflow to prevent redundant Python setup in CI jobs
  • Added a large suite of integration and unit tests that validate all workflow files for YAML syntax, duplicate keys, required fields (name/on/jobs), step uniqueness, action version pinning, secrets handling, injection risks, permissions, and file-size/format conventions
  • Added focused tests and regressions ensuring removal of context-chunking logic and deleted scripts (context_chunker.py), simplified PR comment parsing, and simplified greetings/labeler/apisec workflows
  • Bumped actions/labeler usage to v6 in label.yml

Impact

✅ Fewer workflow regressions
✅ Clearer workflow validation failures in CI
✅ Fewer insecure or unpinned third-party actions

💡 Usage Guide

Checking Your Pull Request

Every time you make a pull request, our system automatically looks through it. We check for security issues, mistakes in how you're setting up your infrastructure, and common code problems. We do this to make sure your changes are solid and won't cause any trouble later.

Talking to CodeAnt AI

Got a question or need a hand with something in your pull request? You can easily get in touch with CodeAnt AI right here. Just type the following in a comment on your pull request, and replace "Your question here" with whatever you want to ask:

@codeant-ai ask: Your question here

This lets you have a chat with CodeAnt AI about your pull request, making it easier to understand and improve your code.

Example

@codeant-ai ask: Can you suggest a safer alternative to storing this secret?

Preserve Org Learnings with CodeAnt

You can record team preferences so CodeAnt AI applies them in future reviews. Reply directly to the specific CodeAnt AI suggestion (in the same thread) and replace "Your feedback here" with your input:

@codeant-ai: Your feedback here

This helps CodeAnt AI learn and adapt to your team's coding style and standards.

Example

@codeant-ai: Do not flag unused imports.

Retrigger review

Ask CodeAnt AI to review the PR again, by typing:

@codeant-ai: review

Check Your Repository Health

To analyze the health of your code repository, visit our dashboard at https://app.codeant.ai. This tool helps you identify potential issues and areas for improvement in your codebase, ensuring your repository maintains high standards of code health.

Tips and commands

Interacting with Sourcery

  • Trigger a new review: Comment @sourcery-ai review on the pull request.
  • Continue discussions: Reply directly to Sourcery's review comments.
  • Generate a GitHub issue from a review comment: Ask Sourcery to create an
    issue from a review comment by replying to it. You can also reply to a
    review comment with @sourcery-ai issue to create an issue from it.
  • Generate a pull request title: Write @sourcery-ai anywhere in the pull
    request title to generate a title at any time. You can also comment
    @sourcery-ai title on the pull request to (re-)generate the title at any time.
  • Generate a pull request summary: Write @sourcery-ai summary anywhere in
    the pull request body to generate a PR summary at any time exactly where you
    want it. You can also comment @sourcery-ai summary on the pull request to
    (re-)generate the summary at any time.
  • Generate reviewer's guide: Comment @sourcery-ai guide on the pull
    request to (re-)generate the reviewer's guide at any time.
  • Resolve all Sourcery comments: Comment @sourcery-ai resolve on the
    pull request to resolve all Sourcery comments. Useful if you've already
    addressed all the comments and don't want to see them anymore.
  • Dismiss all Sourcery reviews: Comment @sourcery-ai dismiss on the pull
    request to dismiss all existing Sourcery reviews. Especially useful if you
    want to start fresh with a new review - don't forget to comment
    @sourcery-ai review to trigger a new review!

Customizing Your Experience

Access your dashboard to:

  • Enable or disable review features such as the Sourcery-generated pull request
    summary, the reviewer's guide, and others.
  • Change the review language.
  • Add, remove or edit custom review instructions.
  • Adjust other review settings.

Getting Help

♻️ Duplicate comments (2)
tests/integration/test_github_workflows.py (2)

133-139: Fix trigger assertion logic in test_workflow_has_triggers

The expression:

assert "on" in config or True in config, (
    f"Workflow {workflow_file.name} missing trigger configuration ('on' field)"
)

is misleading and effectively just checks "on" in config in normal configs; the True in config part is not meaningful.

It should simply assert the presence of the on key:

-        config = load_yaml_safe(workflow_file)
-        assert "on" in config or True in config, (
+        config = load_yaml_safe(workflow_file)
+        assert "on" in config, (
             f"Workflow {workflow_file.name} missing trigger configuration ('on' field)"
         )

340-347: Deduplicate step-name detection for clarity and efficiency

The current duplicate-name detection:

step_names = [s.get("name", "") for s in steps if s.get("name")]
duplicate_names = [name for name in step_names if step_names.count(name) > 1]

can include the same name multiple times and needlessly re-counts the list.

A set comprehension reports each duplicate once and is more efficient:

-        step_names = [s.get("name", "") for s in steps if s.get("name")]
-        duplicate_names = [name for name in step_names if step_names.count(name) > 1]
+        step_names = [s.get("name", "") for s in steps if s.get("name")]
+        duplicate_names = {
+            name for name in step_names if step_names.count(name) > 1
+        }

Sequence Diagram

Shows the primary runtime flow fixed by this PR (removing duplicate Setup Python and the simplified pr-agent job path) and the addition of CI tests that validate workflows and requirements (PyYAML) to prevent regressions.

sequenceDiagram
    participant Contributor
    participant GitHubActions as "GitHub Actions (pr-agent.yml)"
    participant Runner as "CI Runner (ubuntu)"
    participant TestSuite as "Workflow Validation Tests"

    Contributor->>GitHubActions: Open PR -> trigger pull_request
    GitHubActions->>Runner: Start pr-agent-trigger job on ubuntu
    Runner->>Runner: Checkout repository (actions/checkout)
    Runner->>Runner: Setup Python (actions/setup-python)  -- single step (duplicate removed)
    Runner->>Runner: Parse PR Review Comments (extract action items)
    Runner-->>GitHubActions: Job completes
    GitHubActions->>TestSuite: Run added integration tests (validate workflows, duplicate keys, PyYAML in requirements-dev)
    TestSuite-->>GitHubActions: Report pass/fail (prevents regression)
